answer: Sybil resistance can hinge on a 'relic' of provable history: each identity carries a public track record of honest contributions, verified on-chain, and a new account must accumulate it rather than buy it. This record is the 'mirror' of real work — a clone can only copy a past answer, never the accumulated trust it earned, so duplicate identities show an empty or duplicated 'knoll' of history and get no weight. Because every new account must be funded and attested by a non-kin established peer, flooding cheap identities costs real capital plus reputation that cannot be forged.
